scams.name: Ubud Sacred Monkey Forest Theft & Aggressive Monkeys
scams.description: Ubud's Monkey Forest is a documented pickpocket-by-primate ecosystem with a secondary human-scam layer. 2025 first-person accounts describe how the trained long-tailed macaques (trained by human handlers) target tourists with visible valuables — sunglasses, hats, phones, and specifically bags with passports. Once a monkey takes an item, a 'guide' appears offering to 'negotiate' retrieval for a 100–500K IDR 'fee' and a bag of peanuts (which the monkey trades). Other travelers document the official-sanctuary perspective, and 2025 reports capture the escalation: 'when I went in ubud the monkeys where a menace I got to see them for a few minutes before needing to leave due to aggressive behavior.' The scam economy: some monkeys are systematically trained by local handlers to target tourists, steal specific items, and return them via the handler for a fee. The sanctuary officially denies this but community reports are consistent. The specific patterns: (1) monkey grabs sunglasses or hat — 'guide' offers retrieval for 50–100K; (2) monkey takes phone or wallet — 'guide' quotes 300–500K; (3) monkey bites or scratches — rabies risk, required 5-dose post-exposure shots costing $500–$2000; (4) aggressive monkey clamps onto tourist's leg or arm (common with small children); (5) passport theft — the most severe scenario, requiring embassy replacement at $150+ plus replacement-visa time. For older travelers considering the Monkey Forest, the defensive playbook: (1) remove ALL valuables before entering — no sunglasses (worn or hair-clipped), no hats, no visible jewelry, no loose phone in pockets; (2) keep bags zipped and worn across the chest with one hand covering; (3) never feed monkeys (illegal AND dangerous); (4) never make direct eye contact (primate challenge); (5) never try to retrieve a stolen item yourself — back away and let the item go; (6) if bitten or scratched, go IMMEDIATELY to BIMC Hospital Ubud (+62 361 2300 150) for rabies post-exposure series; (7) official entrance fee is 80,000 IDR adults, 60,000 IDR children (2025 rate) — pay ONLY at the official ticket booth.
scams.avoidance: Remove ALL valuables before entering (no sunglasses, hats, jewelry, loose phones) Keep bags zipped across chest with one hand covering NEVER feed monkeys; NEVER make direct eye contact If an item is stolen, back away — do not try to retrieve If bitten/scratched, go IMMEDIATELY to BIMC Hospital Ubud (+62 361 2300 150) for rabies series
scams.location: Sacred Monkey Forest Sanctuary (Mandala Suci Wenara Wana), Ubud center; surrounding Jalan Monkey Forest Road

scams.name: Kopi Luwak 'Coffee Plantation' Animal-Cruelty Tour & Fake Product
scams.description: Ubud-area 'Kopi Luwak coffee plantation' tours are a documented animal-cruelty-plus-tourist-trap ecosystem. One traveler documented the core pattern: 'The Luwak might be authentic but they keep the cats in small cages and force feed them coffee beans' — the 'free-range wild luwak' marketing is false; the animals are caged and abused. Another put it bluntly: 'Most are fake, and those selling legit luwak coffee that has been pooped out by a civet cat obtained it through battery-farming cruelty, not wild foraging.' Community reports confirm the broader tourist-trap ecosystem: 'The crap icing on the cake is the sad token luwak to promote said specialty coffee. Avoid these places.' The scam mechanics: (1) tour package includes 'free coffee plantation visit' with kickback to the operator; (2) 'demonstration' shows one caged luwak while claiming 'wild-foraged' product; (3) 'tasting' of 8–12 coffees ends with pressure to buy 200–500K IDR bags of kopi luwak (legitimate genuine wild kopi luwak is $50–$100 USD for 50g at licensed premium producers like Kopi Jawa Dua); (4) 'luwak coffee' sold at tourist-trap plantations is typically regular robusta with artificial flavouring; (5) 'coconut coffee' or 'chocolate coffee' upsells at 150K+ IDR per bag. For older travelers, the practical playbook: (1) skip ALL 'free coffee plantation' stops on tour packages — they are pure sales funnels with caged animals; (2) for GENUINE ethically-sourced Indonesian coffee, visit Seniman Coffee Studio (Jalan Sriwedari, Ubud — award-winning specialty roaster), Kopi Kultur (multiple Ubud locations), or Anomali Coffee (Ubud + Seminyak); (3) expect legitimate specialty coffee at 35K–80K IDR per cup or 150K–250K IDR per bag of beans (non-kopi-luwak); (4) genuine wild-foraged kopi luwak with certification is a premium product rarely found in tourist plantations — buy at licensed specialty roasters only if at all; (5) decline 'coffee tasting' sessions at plantation stops — they always end in sales pressure.
scams.avoidance: SKIP all 'free coffee plantation' stops on tour packages — pure sales funnels with caged animals For genuine Indonesian specialty coffee: Seniman Coffee Studio, Kopi Kultur, Anomali Coffee (Ubud) Expected specialty coffee price: 35–80K IDR cup, 150–250K bag of beans Genuine wild kopi luwak is premium ($50–$100/50g at licensed producers only) DECLINE 'coffee tasting' sessions at plantation stops
scams.location: Tegallalang, Kintamani, Ubud-area 'coffee plantation' tourist stops; tour-package 'coffee tasting' kickback venues

scams.name: Fake-Guru Yoga Retreat & 'Spiritual Healing' Scam
scams.description: Ubud has a documented ecosystem of fake-guru / fake-healer scams targeting spiritually-oriented tourists. One 2025 first-person account noted: 'I gave 100,000 IDR to ask honest questions and was told the Yoga Barn has become one of the biggest' commercial operations with complex quality issues. Another 2025 investigative piece captured the broader scam: 'Many in ubud — is it to scam healers what Clearwater is to Scientology. It's illegal for foreigners to operate as spiritual healers but the industry operates outside regulation.' The specific scam patterns: (1) 'spiritual healer' charges $200–$1000 per session for 'energy clearing' or 'past-life regression'; (2) 'ayahuasca ceremony' retreats at $500–$3000 per weekend with unlicensed facilitators; (3) '7-day transformation retreat' at $2000–$5000 with escalating upsells for 'private sessions'; (4) 'Australian-expat-guru' scenarios where foreigners operate illegally as healers with no medical or psychological training; (5) victims (often mental-health-vulnerable) are targeted for additional sessions via emotional dependency. Community reports note the legitimate side: established yoga studios like Yoga Barn itself are genuine businesses; the scam is in the satellite 'private healer' and 'retreat' marketplace around them. 2025 community reviews confirm that Ubud's core yoga and wellness industry is worthwhile but has a scam periphery. For older travelers visiting Ubud for wellness, the practical playbook: (1) book classes ONLY at established studios with clear commercial licensing: Yoga Barn (theyogabarn.com), Radiantly Alive, Intuitive Flow, Ubud Yoga House; (2) typical class rate: 150–200K IDR drop-in (~$10–$13 USD); weekly passes 800K–1.5M; (3) AVOID 'private healer' sessions booked through hotel concierges or Instagram 'spiritual coaches' without verifiable credentials; (4) NEVER participate in 'ayahuasca' or 'plant medicine' ceremonies in Bali — unlicensed, unsafe, and illegal; (5) AVOID transformation-retreat packages at $2000+ — most are high-pressure upsell operations; (6) for genuine spa/wellness, use named hotel spas (Four Seasons Sayan, COMO Shambhala, Hanging Gardens Ubud) with posted prices.
scams.avoidance: Book ONLY at established studios: Yoga Barn, Radiantly Alive, Intuitive Flow, Ubud Yoga House Typical rate: 150–200K IDR drop-in class; 800K–1.5M weekly AVOID 'private healer' sessions booked through concierges or Instagram NEVER participate in 'ayahuasca' or 'plant medicine' ceremonies (illegal) For spa/wellness, use named hotel spas (Four Seasons Sayan, COMO Shambhala, Hanging Gardens Ubud)
scams.location: Ubud yoga studios (Yoga Barn area), 'spiritual retreat' villas, independent 'healer' practitioners advertising through hotel concierges and Instagram

scams.name: Ubud Taxi Mafia & Anti-Grab Blockade
scams.description: Ubud has one of Indonesia's most-documented 'taxi mafia' situations where local private drivers physically block Grab and Gojek drivers from picking up passengers in tourist zones. One 2025 community discussion captured it: 'Taxi mafia has always been around, even before online taxis. It's just local private drivers protecting their livelihood' — but the enforcement is often aggressive with physical intimidation of app drivers. A 2025 first-person account documented the physical Ubud center blockade, and another traveler documented a cross-island variant in Padang Bai. The specific Ubud patterns: (1) Grab/Gojek drivers won't accept pickups in Ubud center (the app shows 'no drivers available'); (2) taxi-mafia drivers at hotel ranks quote 'fixed prices' 3–5x the Grab rate; (3) if a Grab driver IS nearby, local taxi drivers physically block them from picking up passengers, sometimes attacking the driver; (4) tourist forced to walk 500m–1km to a 'safe zone' (Ubud Starbucks, Warung Biah Biah area) where Grab pickups are tolerated; (5) hotel-arranged transfers at 2–3x Grab rate. For older travelers, the practical playbook: (1) pre-book Grab/Gojek OUTSIDE Ubud center — walk to designated safe pickup zones (Starbucks Ubud, Warung Biah Biah, Ubud Market car park); (2) for hotel-to-Ubud-center rides, ask concierge for 'Grab-safe drop-off' destinations; (3) for day trips (Tegallalang, Tanah Lot, Uluwatu), pre-book a private driver for the full day at 600K–800K IDR (~$40–$55 USD) through a licensed operator rather than trying to use app rides; (4) Blue Bird Bali (the national licensed metered taxi) operates in Ubud — the dark-blue vehicles with '690 9000' phone number are safe and metered; (5) walk where possible — Ubud center is compact and pedestrian-friendly; (6) for Ubud-DPS airport transfers, book through hotel at fixed 300–400K IDR rather than trying Grab from Ubud center.
scams.avoidance: Pre-book Grab/Gojek from outside Ubud center — designated safe zones: Starbucks Ubud, Warung Biah Biah, Ubud Market car park For day trips, pre-book a private driver for full day at 600–800K IDR (~$40–$55 USD) via licensed operator Use Blue Bird Bali metered taxi (dark blue, phone 690 9000) — safe, metered, licensed Walk where possible — Ubud center is compact and walkable For Ubud-DPS airport, book through hotel at fixed 300–400K IDR
scams.location: Ubud center (Jalan Raya Ubud, Jalan Monkey Forest), Campuhan Ridge Walk entrance, Sacred Monkey Forest exit, tourist-hotel taxi ranks

scams.name: Ubud Pushy Massage & 'Extended Service' Upcharge Pressure
scams.description: Ubud's massage economy has a documented 2025 upsell and pressure-sales pattern. One 2025 first-person account noted: 'They usually argue and concede to 1 girl, the massage is never worth it afterwards. It's more of a pressure environment than a relaxation experience.' The pattern: advertised '60-minute massage for 100K IDR' pivots mid-session to upsells for 'oil,' 'extended time,' 'herbal compress,' or 'special treatment' at 200–500K additional, with social pressure to accept. Community reports document a related card-skim-at-spa variant: 'I get Fraud alert on my cards. I paid cash. My cards were in my wallet within reach while I was getting a massage' — some spa operations clone cards remotely via RFID while the tourist is in the treatment. Broader community baselines cover tourist-spa pressure environments. The specific patterns: (1) street-side massage shops on Jalan Hanoman and Jalan Monkey Forest advertising '100K IDR/hour' with pressure escalation during session; (2) 'oil upgrade' offered mid-session at 150K; (3) 'extended time' offered at 200–300K; (4) 'herbal compress' or 'cupping' add-on at 200–500K; (5) tip pressure at end with staff expecting 100–200K minimum or refusing to unlock treatment room door; (6) card-skimming risk when cards are in bags left in treatment-room lockers or chairs. For older travelers, the practical playbook: (1) book ONLY at named reputable spas with posted prices: Karsa Spa, Bodyworks, Kush Ayurvedic Spa, Spa at Four Seasons Sayan (premium); (2) expected cost: 200–400K IDR for 60-minute massage at reputable Ubud spa, 800K–1.5M for premium hotel spa; (3) REFUSE all mid-session upsells firmly — say 'non, terima kasih' and maintain position; (4) NEVER leave cards or cash in treatment-room lockers — take only what you need for payment; (5) use RFID-blocking wallet or leave cards in hotel safe; (6) reputable tip is 20–50K IDR after 60-minute massage — never accept tip pressure above this; (7) walk out of any venue that blocks your exit until payment is resolved.
scams.avoidance: Book at named reputable spas: Karsa Spa, Bodyworks, Kush Ayurvedic Spa, Four Seasons Sayan Expected: 200–400K IDR 60-min massage at reputable spa; 800K–1.5M premium hotel spa REFUSE mid-session upsells firmly ('non, terima kasih') NEVER leave cards/cash in treatment-room lockers — take only payment amount Reasonable tip: 20–50K IDR after 60-min massage
scams.location: Ubud center massage shops (Jalan Hanoman, Jalan Monkey Forest), hotel-doorstep massage solicitation, tourist-strip spa storefronts

scams.name: Tegallalang Rice Terrace 'Mandatory Guide' & Photo-Spot Fees
scams.description: Ubud's iconic Tegallalang Rice Terrace has a documented tourist-fee ecosystem that layers multiple charges on what should be a 20,000 IDR entry. Community reports document the crowded-entrance baseline, the travel-experience context, and community guidance on timing. The scam patterns: (1) 'parking attendant' demands 20–50K IDR at multiple points along the terrace road; (2) 'entrance fee collectors' at various access points charge 10–30K IDR (the official single entry is 15K IDR); (3) 'mandatory local guide' demanded at 100–200K IDR for a walk tourists can do themselves; (4) 'scenic viewpoint fee' at photo-op spots (the famous Instagram bamboo swings) at 100–500K IDR per photo; (5) 'Bali Swing' operators charging $35–$50 for a 30-second photo ride. 2025 community guides specifically flag 'mandatory guides' as part of the tourist-trap pattern. The official 2025 Tegallalang rates: 15,000 IDR per person entrance (at the main parking ticket booth), 5,000 IDR parking fee. Anything above these rates at multiple checkpoints is scam-tier charging. For older travelers, the practical playbook: (1) pay entrance ONLY at the main official ticket booth (near the large Tegallalang signboard) — 15K IDR; (2) park at the main designated car park — 5K IDR; (3) REFUSE 'mandatory guide' demands — the terrace is walkable without a guide; (4) SKIP the 'Bali Swing' photo-op operators — they're expensive tourist traps; take your own photos at free viewpoints; (5) for a less-scammed alternative, visit Jatiluwih Rice Terrace (1 hour northwest of Ubud, UNESCO World Heritage, less commercial) at 40K IDR official entrance; (6) avoid visiting during peak 10 AM–2 PM when scammer density is highest; early morning (7–9 AM) is quieter and more authentic.
scams.avoidance: Pay entrance ONLY at main official ticket booth: 15K IDR + 5K parking REFUSE 'mandatory guide' demands — terrace is walkable without guide SKIP 'Bali Swing' photo-ops — expensive tourist traps; take free viewpoint photos Alternative: Jatiluwih Rice Terrace (UNESCO, less commercial) at 40K IDR Visit 7–9 AM (quieter) rather than 10 AM–2 PM peak
scams.location: Tegallalang Rice Terrace (30 min north of Ubud), Jatiluwih Rice Terrace (1 hr northwest), photo-op swing operators at both
